name: Mohamed Ramadan
description: Mohamed Ramadan writes about economics, finance, leadership and artificial intelligence: where capital goes, why it moves, and what it changes for the people and institutions it touches.
bio: Mohamed Ramadan writes about economics, finance, leadership and artificial intelligence: where capital goes, why it moves, and what it changes for the people and institutions it touches.

He previously served as Chief Financial Officer, and before that as a financial analyst alongside banks and advisory firms. He holds a master's degree in supply chain management from Université Paris-Panthéon-Assas, as well as a master's in finance and accounting and a bachelor's in business administration.

What drives him is curiosity, the habit of asking why a number moved before deciding what it means, and humility, because markets humble everyone and good analysis starts by admitting what we do not know.
Beyond finance, he is a co-founder of YouthShare Initiatives, an aid association. Away from the markets, he loves the mountains and hiking.
why_title: Finance is too important to be left to jargon.
why: Every rate decision, every bond auction, every data centre built with borrowed money ends up in someone's salary, rent or business plan. I write to understand these choices, and to make them understandable.

I write with curiosity, because the most useful question in economics is still why, and with humility, because markets correct anyone who is too sure of themselves. And I write from Africa as much as from London or New York, because the next chapters of the global economy will not be written only in the old capitals.
This is my notebook: analyses, opinion, essays, charts and the words of others that shape my thinking. The views are my own. Disagreement is welcome.
